items.q: Reserving space for ads in the page layout helps reduce layout shift.
items.why: When the space is already set aside, the page does not jump when the ad arrives.

items.q: Loading every ad script before anything else always makes a page faster.
items.why: Heavy scripts delay the content. Loading important content first usually feels faster.

items.q: A consent management platform records a visitor’s privacy choices and passes them on.
items.why: It shows the choices to the visitor and shares the result with ad partners.

items.q: An ads.txt file can be placed on any page of a website.
items.why: It must sit at the root of the domain so buyers know where to look.

items.q: Ads placed where people spend time reading can have better viewability.
items.why: More time in view means more ads count as viewable.

items.q: Infinite scroll can create more ad slots as the visitor keeps scrolling.
items.why: Each new batch of content can carry new ad slots.

items.q: A header bidding timeout is the longest the page waits for bidders before moving on.
items.why: After the timeout, late bids are ignored.

items.q: A longer header bidding timeout always earns more.
items.why: Waiting longer slows the page and gives smaller extra gains, so the best setting is a balance.

items.q: Server-side header bidding moves some of the auction work from the browser to a server.
items.why: That can lighten the page but can make matching users harder.

items.q: Only above-the-fold ads can ever be viewable.
items.why: An ad further down the page is viewable when the visitor scrolls to it.
